analysis: The supplied units are base-side text excerpts (lines 33342-34945) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, a golden-vector test fixture. The excerpts show gpt-oss-20b vectors (endpoint_responses, exact_block_multiple, gemma, gemma_tool_turn and the start of harmony) with token_ids, plan.prompt_contract_id, block_boundaries and chain_hash values. The file_changes patch excerpt, which is truncated, shows head changes elsewhere in the file. They include an added additional_context.enable_thinking=false member, a changed prompt_token_count (803 to 767), changed chain hashes and token_ids for a different vector near base lines 3017-3082, and further small changed ranges later in the file. This is a data-only fixture with no executable code, key material or secrets, and no authorization, attestation or encryption logic. No new attack surface or weakening of provider-side controls (TB-002, TB-011, T-041) is visible. Possible indirect relevance is to the prefix-cache threat T-041, because prompt_contract_id and chain_hash values determine cache keys. A prompt-contract change would invalidate or rotate cached prefix identities rather than create cross-tenant sharing. Whether the production code that consumes these vectors (prompt rendering, additional_context handling, cache key derivation) preserves the tenant scoping and request-trait gating in T-041 is not visible here. The head-side hunks and the consuming source files were not supplied, so that cannot be confirmed. Regenerated vectors should be verified against the code changes in the same PR. I identified no concrete security regression from the supplied evidence.
